messages.author: 2fdab239c1396fa6
messages.subject: Trouble Compiling Zero-Inflated Likelihood Function
parts:
Hello there, I am a PhD student using nimble to develop hidden Markov and hidden semi-Markov rainfall models.

This is a simplest version I can come up with of the problem I am having with the compiler. Suppose I have a vector of n values from a mixture distribution of a Bernoulli(1-p) and some positive distribution e.g. Exponential(theta):

0 , 1.54439307 , 0.12542128 , 0 , 0.52887174 , 0.98874485 , 0 , 0.02455954 , 0 , 0 , ...

The probability densities for these values are given by:

p(x|theta,p)=          p if x=0
                              (1-p)*dexp(x,theta) if x>0

This is straightforward to implement in nimble using a nimbleFunction with if statements and a for loop over the vector of x values. However, in R this can instead be written as:

dens = p*(x==0) + (1-p)*dexp(x,theta)*(x>0)

However, the compiler doesn't seem to manage this version (failed to create the shared library). If the vector of values is very long then the for loop is much slower. In my particular case, it takes 4-5 seconds to evaluate the non-compiled function with a loop in R, compared to 2-3 seconds if it is written as above. I've tried to solve this several times over a last few months, as my knowledge of nimble improves, but I haven't found a solution yet. Here's some code if anyone is interested in trying to reproduce my problem. If anyone is able to get this model to work without using a loop then it would go some way to helping me solve my own problem, for which I would be very grateful!

Thank you!


p <- 0.8
theta <- 1
N <- 1000
x <- rexp(N,theta)*rbinom(N,1,1-p)

dziexp <- nimbleFunction(run=function(x=double(1),p=double(0),theta=double(0),N=double(0),log=integer(0)){
  returnType(double(0))
  return(sum(log(p*(x==0) + (1-p)*dexp(x,theta)*(x>0))))
})

rziexp <- nimbleFunction(run=function(n=integer(0),p=double(0),theta=double(0),N=double(0)){
  returnType(double(1))
  return(rexp(N,1)*rbinom(N,1,1-p))
})

registerDistributions(list(
  dziexp = list(
    BUGSdist = 'dziexp(p,theta,N)',
    types = c('value=double(1)','p=double(0)','theta=double(0)','N=double(0)'),
    mixedSizes = TRUE
  )
))

ziCode <- nimbleCode({
  x[1:n]~dziexp(p,theta,n)
  p~dunif(0,1)
  theta~dunif(0,10)
})

ziConsts <- list(n=N)
ziData <- list(x=x)
ziInits <- list(p=0.5,theta=1)

ziModel <- nimbleModel(ziCode, ziConsts,ziData,ziInits)
ziCModel <- compileNimble(ziModel,resetFunctions = TRUE)

zimcmcConf <- configureMCMC(ziModel,monitors=c('theta','p'),useConjugacy = FALSE)
zimcmcConf$removeSamplers('theta')
zimcmcConf$addSampler('theta',type='slice')

zimcmc<-buildMCMC(zimcmcConf)
ziCmcmc<-compileNimble(zimcmc, project = ziModel,resetFunctions = TRUE)
ziSamples<-runMCMC(ziCmcmc,
                      nchains = 2, nburnin=500,niter = 1000,samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE,
                      summary = FALSE, WAIC = FALSE)
plot(ziSamples)

messages.subject: Re: Trouble Compiling Zero-Inflated Likelihood Function
parts:
Hi Oliver,

Thanks for this.

I'll look more carefully, but to give you a quick answer now, I think the compiler is glitching on the expression involving logicals.  The following looks like it works, but please verify:

dziexp <- nimbleFunction(run=function(x=double(1),p=double(0),theta=double(0),N=double(0),log=integer(0)){
    returnType(double(0))
    x0 <- x==0
    return(sum(log(p*x0 + (1-p)*dexp(x,theta)*(!x0))))
})

Also the registerDistributions should no longer be necessary, unless there are unexpected types.

-Perry
